raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, so every bag of fertilizer matters. I do not make big changes unless I see it work nearby. For wheat, I will follow what I used last year and what the better fields around me are doing: an improved wheat seed, enough base fertilizer, then one topdressing at jointing. Wheat cannot be starved, because if the seedlings are weak in winter or the heads are small in spring, I cannot get that yield back. Since I have well water, I will water wheat about 3 times if the year is normal: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at filling. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed because the yield is steadier and most people around me plant hybrid now. Maize eats fertilizer hard, so I will not be stingy with nitrogen. I will put part below and part as topdressing around the big flare stage, then water 2 times if rain is short. My farm is small and there are only 2 people at home, with some off-farm work, so I will keep things simple: rotary tillage, ordinary herbicide and insect control, and no fancy extra operations. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain. If prices rise too much, I will cut a little potassium first, but I will keep nitrogen and irrigation in place.
